title: Permit a `type` attribute for the `code` tag, to embed IANA Media Types.

labels.name: needs implementer interest
labels.description: Moving the issue forward requires implementers to express interest

body:
### What problem are you trying to solve? Say that I have: ~~~HTML URI List 
            
                https://example.com/0
                https://example.com/1
~~~ As BCP 47 corroborates, ISO 639-2 does not include technical language type, for that's obviously the purpose of IANA's Media Types. However, there is no way to encode this in a `` tag, despite its purpose being to encapsulate all code. [^1] [^1]: [`datatracker.ietf.org/doc/rfc5646/#:~:text=5.%20%20%5BISO639%2D2%5D%20has%20defined%20several,agreement)%20private%20use%20subtags`](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/rfc5646/#:~:text=5.%20%20%5BISO639%2D2%5D%20has%20defined%20several,agreement\)%20private%20use%20subtags.) ### What solutions exist today? 1. #### `language-`-Prefixed CSS3 Classes [`html.spec.whatwg.org/#the-code-element:classes`](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#the-code-element:classes:~:text=There%20is%20no%20formal%20way,with%20%22language%2D%22%20to%20the%20element.) states: [^3] > There is no formal way to indicate the language of computer code being marked up. Authors who wish to mark [code](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#the-code-element) elements with the language used, e.g. so that syntax highlighting scripts can use the right rules, can use the [class](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#classes) attribute, e.g. by adding a class prefixed with "`language-`" to the element. Were the language names standardised, this would be *suitable*, especially because CSS3 class names are able to support every character except null. [^6]. However, this isn't intuitive for an author. [^7] [^6]: [`stackoverflow.com/revisions/6732899/8`](https://stackoverflow.com/revisions/6732899/8#content:~:text=Any%20character%20except%20NUL%20is,for%20CSS%20or%20HTML).%20Done.) [^7]: [`stackoverflow.com/revisions/28107458/3`](https://stackoverflow.com/revisions/28107458/3#content:~:text=you%20can%20use%20attribute%20selectors) [^3]: [`stackoverflow.com/revisions/39549633/3`](https://stackoverflow.com/revisions/39549633/3#content:~:text=In%20the%20WHATWG%E2%80%99s%20HTML%20Living,and%20actually%20implement%20this%20prefix.)) 1. #### Unstandardised, But Compliant, Extension Of Special-Use ISO 639-3 Tags The disadvantages are numerous: 1. I could append the relevant Media Type subtag to the `mis` prefix, like `mis-yaml`, but unlike CSS3 class names, that's not nearly as versatile as a Media Type subtag (ISO 369 wouldn't handle `+yaml`). 1. Additionally, although outside the remit of the WHATWG, this isn't yet handled well by implementers, per [`bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=1971543#c0`](https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=1971543#c0:~:text=Applying%20a%20custom%20font%2Dsize%20to,preference%20is%20not%20adhered%20to.). Regardless, an example of this would be ``. 1. #### Misuse Of Existent Tags I can, *non-semantically*, add a `` tag inside the ``, like `https://example.com`. It doesn't have much purpose, though, except to the markup author (which is better served by a comment). ### How would you solve it? Were a `type` attribute added to ``, `` would be possible. [^2] [^2]: [`iana.org/assignments/media-types/media-types.xhtml#:~:text=%5BRFC5109%5D-,uri%2Dlist,%5BRFC2483%5D,-vcard`](https://www.iana.org/assignments/media-types/media-types.xhtml#:~:text=%5BRFC5109%5D-,uri%2Dlist,%5BRFC2483%5D,-vcard) ### Anything else? I have seen no usage of `type` in `code`, so it should not conflict with established standard.
